tldr: Friday 30 Oct was a sharp risk-off REVERSAL, not a rotation: S&P -1.82%, Nasdaq -2.86% (worst session since June), VIX +12.9% to 19.42 -- triggered by an AI-capex-credibility shock (Intel -28.58% on guidance, worst day since 1974; Amazon's $77B Q3 capex / -$42.4B FCF) layered on Fed speakers Musalem and Logan escalating beyond the hawkish dissent into explicit calls for more hikes.

BIGGEST RISK TO THE BOOK: gold -3.6% to ~$3,885 and silver -5.9% to ~$49.14 (an 11-month low) sold off hard on the same real-yield repricing plus margin-call liquidation spillover from the tech rout -- the 2x levered silver position is now only 8.4% away from its stressed margin-call price after this single session, per the risk log's own 'survivability FAIL' flag.

A record $6.3B Binance hack (the largest crypto theft on record, North-Korea-linked per TRM Labs) hit crypto sentiment on top of the macro shock, pushing Bitcoin to a six-week low near $76,815 and the crypto Fear & Greed Index from 51 to 30 within a day.

China's rare-earth export-control truce stays genuinely unresolved just 10 days from the Nov 10 deadline -- MOFCOM confirmed the broader US-China trade truce runs to Jan 2027 but has published no matching legal text for the rare-earth-specific suspension, keeping MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels a live binary catalyst.

Hong Kong Southbound selling extended to a 12th straight day (~HK$33.8bn cumulative through Oct 29, SMIC the largest net-sell name two sessions running) even before Friday's global risk-off -- a standing headwind for the HK tech sleeve (0700/0981/1810) into Monday's open.

Markets are closed all weekend (next opens: Asia Monday local mornings, US cash Monday 9:30am ET) -- Friday's selloff has not yet had a chance to extend or reverse; weekend geopolitics stayed two-sided (Hormuz tanker-mine attacks at wartime highs vs Qatari-mediated Iran peace talks, Chinese coast guard incursions near Kinmen).
